quantity: median water-equivalent lateral path through the trunk
note: No citable water-equivalent thickness for a lateral lumbar projection exists. The nearest published statement is that rolling a patient from lateral decubitus onto their back adds 2-9 cm of traversed tissue (PMID 23652542). This is measured directly on CT.

quantity: photons per render pixel arriving at the detector
note: 10-70 nGy/frame measured on a Siemens Cios Alpha mobile C-arm (PMID 30339271), converted at 34.2 photons/mm2/nGy over this pixel. The simulator is not fitted to this.

Measured on anthropomorphic AP and lateral abdomen phantoms, where the 95th percentile of the 2-D scatter-to-primary map ran 42 to 185 per cent above its median (PMID 38942002). Compared within one 9-inch field, because that is the region a real measurement covers.

quantity: nearest-neighbour noise correlation at this pixel size
note: A real fluoroscopic panel measures r(1)=0.20 at its own 194 um pitch (PMID 24593724); binning to this render pixel should leave 0.02-0.08, so the band spans both ends. Measured on a FLAT FIELD -- a constant 25.9 cm water path through the same pipeline -- because that is how the published number is measured, on a uniform exposure with nothing in the beam. Off anatomical frames the same quantity reads 0.707, and the difference is real structure finer than the residual kernel counted as grain. This row has been wrong in BOTH directions: a 3x3 median forced it to -0.128 and a wide-kernel residual lifted it to +0.707, and neither was the detector. Any earlier verdict from it, including the receptor blur it was said to have sized, rests on a definition that did not match its source.

quantity: frames where the dose servo runs out of output
ours: 80% of all frames; 100% above 32 cm, 0% below
note: Output must double every 4.2 cm of PMMA (AAPM Report 125 p.27; 4.21 cm measured on a Ziehm mobile C-arm, PMID 34196461), so a real unit runs out on thick patients. This checks the servo pins on the thick side of the ceiling and nowhere else.
After matching mean and standard deviation, so only the shape is compared.

quantity: noise power spectrum shape, log-log correlation, RAW
note: Radially averaged spectrum of the high-pass residual, normalised to unit power. This is the statistic a physics model should get right and a gain-and-gamma augmentation cannot, because it has no mechanism that varies with frequency. RAW means the synthetic frames go in as the detector produced them, while the real panels have been downsampled to a journal column and JPEG compressed -- both low-pass operations acting on exactly the band being measured. The row below is the same comparison with both sides through the same press.

quantity: noise power spectrum shape, log-log correlation, MATCHED
note: The synthetic frames put through downsampling and JPEG before comparing, so both sides have had the same low-pass applied. The difference between this row and the one above is what the PRESS did; whatever remains here is what the detector model owes. Neither row alone answers the question and quoting one would be choosing which question was asked.

quantity: grey-level histogram, total variation distance, MATCHED
note: As above, with the synthetic frames through the journal pipeline.
Panels mined from published figures are 8-bit, JPEG compressed and windowed by someone else. Those without grain are excluded from the noise comparison rather than allowed to flatter it.
